title: P0 hosted API coldstart + backpressure surge retrospective
body:
Executive summary:

On 2026-11-02 16:22 UTC we observed a P0 degradation of the Hosted API affecting streaming responses and short-lived non-streaming requests across eu-west and us-central edges. Symptom set: elevated p95/p99 latency, increased 502/503/500 errors from the model-worker tier, and streaming session stalls/fragmentation. Impact window: ~16:22 to 18:05 UTC with intermittent regressions until mitigations fully rolled out at 19:10 UTC.

Customer impact: ~7% of active customer sessions experienced either truncated streams (client saw stream stop mid-response) or high tail latency (>5s TTFB). A small subset of high-throughput tenants saw elevated 5xx rates for short requests (<=2 tokens).

Low-level summary (TL;DR for on-call):
- Trigger: simultaneous warm-up of cold model caches after a regional deploy + tweak to prefetch heuristic in the multiplexer layer.
- Amplifier: autoscaler spin-up + aggressive prefetch created bursts of KV cache fills and synchronous prefetch eviction churn which increased CPU and memory pressure on the model-worker pool.
- Backpressure bug: the streaming backpressure signal produced by the multiplexer was throttled incorrectly during warm-up, causing acceptor threads to continue accepting requests even while worker queues were saturated. This led to head-of-line blocking, increased RPC timeouts, and 502/503 cascades.

Timeline (reconstructed from telemetry and on-call notes):
- 16:11 UTC: Canary deploy of runtime change that adjusted the prefetch window from 64 tokens to 256 tokens (intended to improve throughput for long-history requests).
- 16:17 UTC: Autoscaler started adding pool capacity in us-central triggered by canary traffic spike.
- 16:22 UTC: Ops alert: p99 latency across streaming endpoints jumped 3x; SLO alert fires. Paging initiated.
- 16:25-16:40 UTC: On-call SRE observed worker CPU saturation and elevated GC. Attempts to retry/kill problematic workers temporarily improved error rate but not tail latency.
- 16:45 UTC: Initial mitigation: roll back prefetch heuristic in canary cluster; this reduced new-session pressure but the global effect remained due to prefix cache thrash.
- 17:05 UTC: Identified backpressure-signal bug in multiplexer (PR reference in linked_artifacts). Hotfix patch applied to edge multiplexer to correctly clamp acceptor when worker queue depth exceeded safe threshold.
- 17:30 UTC: Rolling restart of unhealthy worker pool with controlled warmup (throttled prefetch) began.
- 19:10 UTC: Metrics stable and SLOs recovered.

Root cause analysis:
1) Behavioral change: prefetch window increase (64 -> 256) expands the number of token-prefixes the prefetcher pulls into the KV cache per session, multiplying memory working set at warmup. This was intended for latency improvements on long-horizon prompts but was not validated under cold-cache conditions.
2) Coupled capacity response: autoscaler reacts to short-term CPU signals and starts new instances. New instances start cold, triggering additional prefetch and amplifying cache churn. The combined effect is an order-of-magnitude increase in KV cache fill rate.
3) Backpressure control defect: multiplexer backpressure code uses a leaky-bucket derived signal that was incorrectly reset during initial warmup. Result: acceptor thread continues to accept new multiplexed streams while worker queue depth was above the critical threshold. This created queueing inside workers and head-of-line blocking, leading to timeouts and 5xx escalations.

Contributing factors (secondary):
- Lack of gate in prefetch toggle: change deployed as runtime flag without a canary-specific cold-cache stress test.
- Observability blind spot: we did not have an explicit metric for prefetch fill rate by instance during warmup; we tracked KV cache hit/miss but not evictions per-second per-instance during spin-up.
- Runbook gaps: acceptor clamp playbook existed but referenced an older metrics name; on-call took ~20 minutes to map metric names and escalate.

Immediate mitigations performed (ordered):
- Rolled back prefetch config in canary (16:45) to halt new prefetch pressure.
- Applied hotfix to multiplexer to enforce acceptor clamp at queue depth threshold (17:05).
- Started controlled rolling restart of model-worker pool with a warmup throttle on prefetch (17:30).
- Opened autoscaler cooldown to 5m to prevent immediate re-scaling on transient CPU blips.

Observed effect of mitigations:
- Rollback reduced new cold-cache pressure but residual thrash remained for sessions already in flight.
- Acceptor clamp immediately reduced 5xx spike and allowed queue depths to stabilize.
- Throttled restarts limited simultaneous cache warmups, restoring KV cache working set to sustainable levels.

Post-incident actions (short-term):
- Revert prefetch heuristic change from runtime flag to feature-flagged rollout with staged warmup and chaos/cold-cache validation: Jira SRE-1245 assigned.
- Add a derived metric: instance_prefetch_fill_rate and instance_kv_evictions_per_second (per-worker). Alert when either exceeds threshold during scale events.
- Update autoscaler to consider a warmup mode (scale slowly for instances with low kv-cache-hit-rate).
- Patch multiplexer backpressure logic to use a strictly monotonic queue-depth watermark and add unit tests that simulate warmup resets.
- Run a postmortem blameless review with the runtime and autoscaler owners and product manager.

Long-term preventative work (owner & ETA):
- autoscaler: implement "graceful-warmup" mode (owner: Samir Rao, ETA: 2027-01-15).
- prefetch: gating and canary short-window tests with cold-cache simulation in CI (owner: Lena Wu, ETA: 2026-12-07).
- multiplexer: refactor backpressure into central library with canonical metrics and contract tests (owner: Miguel Torres, ETA: 2026-12-21).
- observability: expose per-instance kv eviction and prefetch counters and create dashboard + SLO alert (owner: eng-observability, ETA: 2026-11-20).

Runbook updates (draft changes):
- Add new play: "Cold-cache scale spike" with steps:
  1. Identify if p99 increase correlates with newly created instances (filter by instance.age < 10m).
  2. Temporarily clamp prefetch globally: set prefetch-window to safe value (64) across affected edges.
  3. If worker queues > clamp threshold, apply acceptor clamp via multiplexer control plane and consider draining affected workers.
  4. If autoscaler is actively scaling, increase cooldown and trigger controlled restart with throttled prefetch.
- Clarify metric names and add quick commands for metric queries (examples included).

On-call quick reference (for future incidents):
- Primary signals to check: p95/p99 latency, instance_prefetch_fill_rate, instance_kv_evictions_per_second, worker_queue_depth_p50/p95, acceptor_accept_rate, model_worker_cpu, model_worker_gc_pause_ms.
- Immediate actions checklist:
  * Toggle prefetch to baseline value in runtime flags
  * Enable acceptor clamp on multiplexer
  * Pause autoscaler (set scale-in/scale-out cooldown to 5m)
  * Start controlled rolling restart of model-workers with warmup throttle enabled

Retrospective notes / open questions:
- Why did autoscaler aggressively scale on short CPU signals without checking cache-hit indicators? (Action: autoscaler team to evaluate inputs).
- Should prefetch be adaptive per-instance rather than global? Tradeoffs: complexity vs latency gains.
- Are there better synthetic tests we can run in CI that accurately model cold-cache warmups at scale?

Appendices (evidence links and snippets):
- Key logs: snippet of multiplexer acceptor counters showing accept_rate not dropping while worker_queue_depth rose (attached in Jira SRE-1245).
- Grafana panels referenced: HostedAPI->Streaming->Prefetch Fill Rate; ModelWorker->Queue Depth; Autoscaler->Scale Events.
- PR: hotfix applied to multiplexer backpressure (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3821).

Authors: Aisha Patel (lead SRE on call), Miguel Torres (runtime), Lena Wu (observability), Samir Rao (autoscaler).

Status: Draft postmortem — collecting a few more logs from eu-west before finalizing.

Notes to self: finish the runbook play snippets and attach the Grafana query templates before we move to final.
